name: Negative Space Portrait Commission — Spire Atrium Series
creator: Yemisi Adeyemi-Brandt, commissioned by Axiom Consolidated Cultural Division
description: A series of twelve monumental holographic portrait installations in Spire corporate atria, each depicting a founding executive of a major corponation — but rendered entirely as absence, the figure visible only as a void in a field of dense luminous particles that swirl around the negative space. The commissions were intended as celebratory monuments; the artist delivered something that reads, to most viewers, as portraits of erasure and void. Axiom Consolidated accepted delivery without comment.
medium: holographic / physical installation / particle field display
cultural_impact: Became the subject of intense critical debate about whether the artist subverted the commission or whether corponation aesthetics had become so comfortable with void imagery that the critique was invisible to its patrons.
controversy: Three of the twelve portrait subjects attempted to have their installations removed after critics widely described the series as 'monuments to the harm powerful people cause by their absence from accountability.' Axiom Consolidated refused removal, citing contract.
story_hooks: One of the portrait subjects dies under suspicious circumstances and the void in their portrait begins to behave anomalously — filling slowly with light in a pattern no technician can explain or stop.
A character hired to maintain the installations discovers a hidden data layer in the particle field code that constitutes a complete record of the subject's financial crimes.
Adeyemi-Brandt is approached to create a thirteenth portrait — of a corponation executive who is still alive and very much wants to know what she sees when she looks at them.
